The method was developed to address the visual limitations of early KRS rendering, specifically the repetitive patterns caused by uniform texturing across symmetric instances [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that 'Texturing all kernel instances with the same coordinates produces an extremely repetitive pattern, emphasizing symmetries undesirably' and recommends applying 'procedural 3D or triplanar texturing to eliminate observable repetitiveness.' This directly supports the claim that the method was developed to address visual limitations (repetitive patterns) caused by uniform texturing across symmetric instances.
supported
It sets itself apart from standard parametric texturing by handling complex or reflective kernels where simple $u,v$ parametrization is not feasible [S1].

The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly states in Section 8.2 (Texturing) that 'The kernel solids are usually simple objects (e.g. torus segments) that lend themselves to easy u, v parametrization.' It then discusses techniques to handle complexity and repetitiveness, noting that procedural or triplanar texturing is applied to eliminate observable repetitiveness, which implies a departure from or limitation of standard simple parametrization for complex cases. The notes further clarify that 'Using u,v parametrization is not feasible if the kernel parametrization is not trivial or if kernels are simplistic (like infinite planes) where details are determined by reflection transformations.' This supports the claim that the method handles complex/reflective kernels where simple u,v parametrization is not feasible, setting it apart from standard approaches.

Transformation chains maintain the composition of Möbius transformations ($\mathcal{L}_{G_i}$) and reflections ($\mathcal{L}_R$) to map world space to kernel space [S1].

The evidence explicitly defines the iteration formula for Möbius kernel-reflection sequences (MöKRS) as $L_{i+1} = L_{G_i}(K_{i+1} ∪ L_i ∪ L_R(L_i))$, where $L_{G_i}$ is a Möbius transformation and $L_R$ is a reflection (also defined as a Möbius transformation in the text). The text further explains that to ray-trace this geometry, the current ray point is transformed with $L_{G_i}$ to symmetry space and then to kernel space with either the identity or $L_R$. This confirms that the transformation chain maintains the composition of these specific transformations to map between spaces.
